rooftops.name: Lantern Supper Roof
rooftops.line: The stalls share their last pot upstairs. Follow the lit stairs to the lanterns; bring your bowl back down when you leave.

rooftops.name: Glass Observatory
rooftops.line: Browse the paper copies outside, then take the stairs to the roof. We compare the sky with the archive's weather records up there.

rooftops.name: Copper Relay Roof
rooftops.line: Repaired couplings leave from the street bench. The stairs lead to our roof relay and the crew's cooling fans.

rooftops.name: Willow Roof Garden
rooftops.line: Take a cutting from the court and carry water up the stairs. The roof beds and rain collectors belong to everyone on this block.

rooftops.name: Last Light Lookout
rooftops.line: Parcels wait under the street shelter. Take the marked stairs to the roof for a seat, a hot drink, and a view of the late connections.

districts.name: AFTERLIGHT COMMONS
districts.subtitle: Night stalls · public terminals · street supply

districts.name: THE GLASS ARCHIVE
districts.subtitle: Vault district · records and cooling towers

districts.name: THE PALE BASIN
districts.subtitle: Dry harbor · salt roads · low visibility

biomes.name: MOURNING FEN
biomes.subtitle: Eastern wetland · pump crews · falling water
biomes.description: Reeds and pools east of Vesper filter the city’s runoff. Mara’s crew earns wages pumping the water, but the extraction is also draining their wells.

biomes.name: CINDERWOOD
biomes.subtitle: Western canopy · cutting crews · ashfall
biomes.description: The surviving trees west of Vesper shelter young growth from the heat. Tovin’s crew is paid to cut them under a restoration program that counts dead seedlings as future timber.

biomes.name: GLASSROOT STEPPE
biomes.subtitle: Northern grassland · ceramic kilns · mineral seam
biomes.description: The northern mineral seam supplies ceramic for Lattice bodies. Digging deeper would undermine the roots around Ada’s settlement and its well.

biomes.name: BRINE BLOOM
biomes.subtitle: Southern salt pans · sealed cultures · abandoned homes
biomes.description: Fungal cultures spread across the southern salt pans. Ilex keeps stable samples sealed while escaped strains consume the seep and force households to leave.

uses.name: Bell Street Clinic
uses.purpose: The clinic keeps two beds free for kitchen workers. The blue cupboard holds donated dressings.
uses.history: A nurse repaired the doorway after the last flood. The old water mark is still on the wall.

uses.name: Second Use Repairs
uses.purpose: Bring broken hotplates to the front counter. Repaired ones go on the shelf by the door.
uses.history: The owner started with one borrowed soldering iron. Neighbors still lend the expensive tools.

uses.name: Mina’s Noodles
uses.purpose: Mina serves broth before the early shift. Used bowls go in the washing crate.
uses.history: The mismatched stools came from three cafes that closed when water prices rose.

uses.name: Carriers Rest
uses.purpose: Couriers leave their carts outside and take turns using the kettle.
uses.history: The cracked station clock is kept ten minutes fast so nobody misses the last lift.

uses.name: The Book Swap
uses.purpose: Leave a book on the return shelf or take one upstairs to read.
uses.history: A retired printer opened the room after the school lost its library.

uses.name: Lantern Washhouse
uses.purpose: Shared washers run in batches to save water. Collect dry clothes upstairs.
uses.history: Families bought the first machine together. Their payment list is pinned beside it.

uses.name: Seed and Stem
uses.purpose: Kitchen scraps feed the seedlings. The sturdy plants go to the upstairs nursery.
uses.history: The first tomato plant grew in a split soup tin. Its cuttings fill the window now.

uses.name: Parcel House
uses.purpose: Deliveries are sorted by street. Unclaimed medicine stays behind the counter.
uses.history: The chalk marks record parcels carried upstairs for neighbors who cannot manage the steps.

uses.name: Voss Memory Clinic
uses.purpose: Patients check a memory copy before the clerk seals it. Appointments are written beside the beds.
uses.history: One cabinet is empty. Its owner chose deletion, and the staff kept the space unassigned.

uses.name: Lens and Coil
uses.purpose: Technicians rebuild the readers that play stored memories. Lenses dry on the padded bench.
uses.history: The oldest reader only works when warm. Staff wrap it in a blanket before the first appointment.

uses.name: The Margins Cafe
uses.purpose: Clerks trade lunch shifts here while their cooling checks run.
uses.history: The tables have pencil notes under their varnish, left by readers before the cafe opened.

uses.name: Witness Waiting Room
uses.purpose: Families wait here while relatives review their records upstairs.
uses.history: Every chair was donated after visitors spent a winter waiting on the pavement.

uses.name: Loose Leaf Library
uses.purpose: Paper copies stay available when the archive network goes down.
uses.history: The handwritten index is longer than the official one. It includes records the city stopped listing.

uses.name: Clean Sleeve Laundry
uses.purpose: The crew washes protective sleeves and clinic bedding separately.
uses.history: The floor tiles mark where cooling equipment stood before the room became a laundry.

uses.name: Glasshouse Cuttings
uses.purpose: Shade plants grow beside the warm archive exhaust. Ask before taking a cutting.
uses.history: A clerk planted the first vine to cover a sealed window. It now reaches the second floor.

uses.name: Witness Post
uses.purpose: Sealed consent forms wait in numbered trays. Clerks collect them in person.
uses.history: The delivery slot was widened so people could send paper records without folding them.

uses.name: Shift Clinic
uses.purpose: The clinic treats burns and keeps spare respirator filters by the entrance.
uses.history: Workers fitted the second doorway so stretchers could pass through without turning.

uses.name: Three Bolt Workshop
uses.purpose: Used heat couplings are tested here before they return to the flats.
uses.history: Three founders welded their first tools to the sign. Only one still works full time.

uses.name: The Relief Canteen
uses.purpose: The incoming crew eats first; the outgoing crew gets food packed for home.
uses.history: The counter is cut from an old freight platform. Its weight limit is still stamped on the edge.

uses.name: Boiler Crew Rooms
uses.purpose: Workers wait for shift assignments and dry their coats by the pipes.
uses.history: The benches face away from the furnace after an apprentice complained about the glare.

uses.name: Repair Manuals
uses.purpose: Borrow a workshop manual or add a correction in the margin.
uses.history: Half the diagrams are hand drawn because the manufacturers no longer supply parts.

uses.name: Copper Wash
uses.purpose: Work clothes soak downstairs. Clean clothes are kept away from the ash upstairs.
uses.history: The crew fitted a second filter after a washer clogged with metal filings.

uses.name: Warm Wall Nursery
uses.purpose: Seed trays use waste heat from the workshop. The water tank is checked each shift.
uses.history: Neighbors started growing greens here during a delivery strike. They kept the beds afterward.

uses.name: Reclaimed Parts Depot
uses.purpose: Couriers sort salvaged valves by size before sending them to repair crews.
uses.history: Each crate names the building it came from, so crews can trace a faulty batch.

uses.name: Court Clinic
uses.purpose: The waiting room uses a light to call patients. Written instructions are available at the desk.
uses.history: Neighbors replaced the loud door buzzer with a lamp after the clinic moved in.

uses.name: Lamp and Rail
uses.purpose: Repairers test the warning lamps and handrail motors here.
uses.history: The first test switch is still mounted low enough for the children who helped wire it.

uses.name: Willow Kitchen
uses.purpose: Meals are collected from the window. The upstairs room is open for shared dinners.
uses.history: The cook keeps the dented stockpot that served the block during the flood.

uses.name: Garden Waiting Room
uses.purpose: Carers rest here between visits. The noticeboard lists who needs a lift home.
uses.history: The long bench was built around a tree root instead of cutting it out.

uses.name: Court Reading Room
uses.purpose: Neighbors borrow books and write replies to the weekly notices.
uses.history: The shelves were made from the frames of removed advertising screens.

uses.name: Reed Laundry
uses.purpose: The laundry saves rinse water for the courtyard planters.
uses.history: Residents moved the drying lines upstairs to keep the entrance clear for wheelchairs.

uses.name: Common Ground Nursery
uses.purpose: Keep the seed trays damp. The marked ones are reserved for flooded courtyards.
uses.history: Each planter carries the name of the household that will look after it.

uses.name: Court Delivery Room
uses.purpose: Groceries wait in shaded boxes until neighbors collect them.
uses.history: A volunteer added a second list for people who need deliveries carried upstairs.

uses.name: Night Connection Clinic
uses.purpose: The night medic treats lift crews and passengers between departures.
uses.history: The examination lamp runs on its own battery after a blackout interrupted a treatment.

uses.name: Cable Service
uses.purpose: Lift brake pads are measured here before each replacement.
uses.history: A retired mechanic marked the safe wear limit on every bench in yellow paint.

uses.name: Last Stop Kitchen
uses.purpose: Hot meals are kept ready for the late connection. Bring containers back on your next shift.
uses.history: The owner changed the opening hours after cleaners repeatedly arrived to a closed counter.

uses.name: Platform Lodge
uses.purpose: Passengers can wait indoors and check the next staffed lift.
uses.history: The folding beds were bought by night workers who missed too many connections home.

uses.name: Travel Reading Room
uses.purpose: Paper timetables and route books stay here when the boards fail.
uses.history: The map includes the service stairs that never appeared on the passenger diagrams.

uses.name: Night Crew Laundry
uses.purpose: Clean uniforms are packed by shift so crews can collect them on the way up.
uses.history: A cleaner painted the delivery shelf numbers large enough to read at the end of a long shift.

uses.name: Cable Garden
uses.purpose: The sheltered nursery supplies plants for the windbreaks on the skyway.
uses.history: The first seedlings were carried up in a mechanic’s lunch box.

uses.name: Late Parcel Office
uses.purpose: Last deliveries wait here for the night lift crew. Medical parcels go first.
uses.history: The wall clock has two hands from different stations, fitted by the overnight repairer.

landmarks.name: Relay terminal
landmarks.evidence: Iri’s route board keeps three columns: delivery promised, delivery received, person checking the next crossing. A salt-stained photograph shows a relief road with drilling rigs on it. She has written CHECK BOTH DIRECTIONS beneath the image.

landmarks.name: Memory vault
landmarks.evidence: A permission record records permission, expiry, and withdrawal separately. Sera’s own first week remains sealed. Its cooling meter turns at the same rate whether the memory is read, copied, or left private.

landmarks.name: Public forge
landmarks.evidence: Bram’s work sheet leaves room for the outgoing crew, the relief crew, and parts still missing. An old inspection stamp fits neatly over the missing-parts column. He keeps the stamped original where apprentices can compare it.

landmarks.name: Warning control panel
landmarks.evidence: The old panel confirms BROADCAST SENT. The replacement asks which lamps, handrails, and receivers actually acknowledged it. Ves has left the failed tests on the board beside the successful ones.

landmarks.name: South floodgate
landmarks.evidence: The outward route plate lists the next water stop and a turnback point. Under an older promise of unlimited deliveries, carriers have scratched the actual capacity of their carts. Someone has kept both readings.

landmarks.name: Last salt beacon
landmarks.evidence: The beacon preserves a call’s source, date, and expiry. Its paper board has room for the reply. One old rescue request repeats across several sheets; an automatic receipt is the only answer attached.

landmarks.name: Public memory archive
landmarks.evidence: A council closing sheet carries total charges, projected output, and penalties in permanent fields. Names, refusals, and interrupted services survive in attached witness notes. Oru’s old clerk mark appears on a copied total with none of its attachments.

landmarks.name: Commons exchange
landmarks.evidence: KITCHEN FEED: LOCKED. MEALS SUPPLIED: 14. The dispatch receipt counts an allocated bowl as a completed meal. Nella has written fourteen names beneath it, each beside an empty place. The water notice preserves every charge but records no missed service.

landmarks.name: Basin listening station
landmarks.evidence: The listening station compares the fen’s water, Cinderwood’s shade, the steppe’s soil, and the bloom’s spread. Each survey names its observer. Blank spaces mean a reading is missing, never that a resource is unlimited.

landmarks.name: Fen water gauge
landmarks.evidence: The high-water stain sits above the current reading. The pump’s delivery counter is still rising. A handwritten sheet compares overtime wages with the depth of the household wells; the best-paid shifts have the steepest drops.

landmarks.name: Company water gate
landmarks.evidence: The company’s proposed shares pay more when withdrawals exceed the wetland limit. They carry no vote over pumping. Clinic demand appears on a separate sheet and remains above summer recharge even without the dividend runs.

landmarks.name: Cinderwood tree records
landmarks.evidence: The same nursery photograph appears on years of restoration certificates. The crew’s pension reserve bought those certificates. Tovin has attached actual seedling-survival counts and his daughter’s next treatment bill.

landmarks.name: Last canopy refuge
landmarks.evidence: Inside the canopy, the soil holds moisture. Outside it, the roots crumble. The maintenance map shows a longer supply route around the living stand and no entry for the cost of losing its shade.

landmarks.name: Glassroot soil core
landmarks.evidence: The core records a mineral seam beneath the settlement’s well. Removing it would provide replacement ceramic and collapse the water-bearing ground. Ada has placed a shell-repair estimate beside the measurements.

landmarks.name: Land ownership records
landmarks.evidence: The survey’s field notes list houses, a kiln, and a well. The valuation removes all three before labeling the land vacant. The offered relocation loans still name the residents it claims are absent.

landmarks.name: Last freshwater seep
landmarks.evidence: Refuge jars and escaped strains draw from the same freshwater seep. Ilex’s dated markers show where households withdrew as the growth advanced. A culture-license notice calls every increase in growth a recovery.

landmarks.name: Sealed culture bank
landmarks.evidence: The licensed strain needs a scarce feed. Its escaped descendants can draw straight from the seep. Sealed jars carry care instructions; the sales ledger treats host survival and unrestricted growth as the same successful delivery.

landmarks.name: Lantern kitchen records
landmarks.evidence: Fourteen bowls went uncollected yesterday. The kitchen still counted them as meals supplied. Beside each bowl, Nella has written the name of someone who could no longer afford water. This is the first page of what Oru will call the Living Record: allotted food is not proof of a meal received.

landmarks.name: Commons water meter
landmarks.evidence: The meter records one household debit and one kitchen debit for every donated jug. The same serial numbers appear in both columns. The company labels the second payment a charitable handling charge.

landmarks.name: Kitchen schedule board
landmarks.evidence: The proposed work schedule assigns purchasing, cooking, washing, and an open weekly count to different households. Donations cannot be billed back to their donors. The water allotment itself remains unchanged.

landmarks.name: Unsorted witness shelf
landmarks.evidence: A sealed request asks to preserve a morning spent repairing a coat with a sister. Its index says commercially insignificant. The witness has not consented to deletion.

landmarks.name: Cooling priority console
landmarks.evidence: The cooling queue sorts by outstanding payments, then by resale eligibility. Consent is recorded in a column the scheduling routine never reads. Three premium cabinets hold redundant copies.

landmarks.name: Glass Steps permission desk
landmarks.evidence: The amended work schedule asks each witness which copies can be released. Cold storage is allocated to irreplaceable records first. It cannot preserve every copy; no clerk may choose a deletion for someone else.

landmarks.name: Occupied flats register
landmarks.evidence: Twenty-three occupied flats are listed as vacant overflow. Their residents have written indoor temperatures beside the official zero population. The former company office receives heat continuously.

landmarks.name: Copper heating valve
landmarks.evidence: The valve can share the office feed between occupied homes. Its default repair form makes the named technician personally liable for eleven years of deferred maintenance.

landmarks.name: Copper Walk shift rules
landmarks.evidence: The rules rotate heat between risers, caps working hours, and records the inherited repair responsibility for payment as contested. No relief worker signs as the sole debtor.

landmarks.name: Court warning log
landmarks.evidence: The last flood advisory reached the advertising amplifier. The amplifier was disconnected by unanimous request. No visual or tactile endpoint acknowledged the warning.

landmarks.name: Handrail warning control
landmarks.evidence: The test circuit pairs an amber lamp sequence with pulses through the handrail. A separate steady light marks a failed circuit. The prototype draws power from the court battery.

landmarks.name: Listening Courts noticeboard
landmarks.evidence: The inspection work schedule names two neighbors per shift and a manual warning route if the battery fails. The lights and handrail stay public; private rooms keep control of their own speakers.

landmarks.name: Night platform register
landmarks.evidence: Forty service-pass holders signed the last departure sheet: cleaners, carers, couriers, and a lift mechanic. The public timetable records no paying passengers and recommends closure.

landmarks.name: Service-pass counter
landmarks.evidence: The occupancy counter excludes service passes before counting passengers. A maintenance company supplies those passes as part of wages. The system treats these passes as wages but leaves their passengers out of the count.

landmarks.name: Last Connection duty board
landmarks.evidence: The revised work schedule staffs the late lift and retains fewer, published connections. Service passes count toward demand. A named relief crew inherits each shift, and missed departures must be recorded.
